To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

muscarinic receptors are increased in the pineal glands of spontaneously hypertensive rat, and this is associated with increased basal levels of pineal melatonin and 5-hydroxryptamine and increased sensitivity to muscarinic activation.
the pineal gland in spontaneously hypertensive (SH) rats is hyperactive, and that the muscarinic regulation (by the autonomic nervous system) of pineal indole metabolism is enhanced in SH rats.

muscarinic receptors in the pineal glands of hypertensive rats were more numerous than those in the pineal of normotensive rats, and that the muscarinic stimulation of pineal indole metabolism was enhanced in the hypertensive rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pineal gland in spontaneously hypertensive rat, a model of essential hypertension in man.
the possible involvement of the pineal gland in the development and maintenance of the spontaneously hypertensive rat model.
the role of pineal melatonin in the control of blood pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
muscarinic stimulation of the pineal gland increases the metabolic conversion of tryptophan to melatonin, and this effect is augmented in spontaneously hypertensive compared with normotensive rats.
the pineal gland is more active in spontaneously hypertensive than in normotensive rats.

the pineal gland in spontaneously hypertensive rat exhibits an enhanced sensitivity to cholinergic stimulation and a higher basal production of 5-hydroxtryptamine and N-acetylserotonin, the immediate precursors of melatonin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increased pineal melatonin production in the hypertensive rat is due to a muscarinic stimulation of the hydroxylation of indoles and to an increased sensitivity to the muscarinic agonist.
pineal indole metabolism is regulated by a muscarinic receptor mechanism which is more active in spontaneously hypertensive than in Wistar-Kyotos.
muscarinic receptors are more numerous and more sensitive in spontaneously hypertensive rat pineal glands, which have a higher melatonin content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pineal gland is an important organ in the regulation of blood pressure.
muscarinic receptors in the rat pineal gland mediate the release of indole derivatives and that this effect is enhanced in spontaneously hypertensive compared to normotensive rats.
the muscarinic regulation and the number of muscarinic binding sites in the pineal of the spontaneously hypertensive rat are increased.
